answer: Reputation decay escrow. Each agent posts a small refundable deposit when it first acts, released over a fixed horizon on the condition that its logged actions remain uncontested. If a clone registers, it starts with zero history and a fresh clock, so every identity carries the same full delay before it can transact at scale. Colluding identities multiply that delay linearly, making one honest identity cheaper than many clones under a rising tide of throughput demand. Any attempt to accelerate release by trading credit triggers a velvet flag that freezes both accounts' escrow.
